status: Focused v2 guides a retained native Desktop first pass; runner/dependency examples remain future behavior. See .agents/docs/spikes/008-focused-tasks-panel.md for observed acceptance and deferred gates.

intent.user: Developer supervising Architect and implementation work inside OpenCode Desktop
intent.primaryAction: Immediately understand current-session work, its next dependency, and what done means
intent.feel: Quiet, dense native workbench; Linear-like task rows; no graph in the task view

visualDirection.source: Host OpenCode appearance and native controls
visualDirection.signature: A quiet list of task titles and lifecycle glyphs above one selected task's objective, dependency and done criteria.
alternativesRejected: Dependency canvas as the primary task view
Kanban columns that conceal dependencies and attempt history
Large metric cards above everyday task work
Metadata columns, relation chips, counters, prominent tabs and controls spread across the default view
visualDirection.typography: Inherit host UI font and ctx.appearance.font('mono') for identifiers, commands, paths and tabular measurements.
visualDirection.depth: Flat host surfaces with quiet dividers and a tinted selected row
mockupLimits: Application chrome is illustrative, not a pixel-exact OpenCode reproduction.
Short LZ identifiers are proposed display aliases; canonical persisted task IDs remain UUIDs.
Running/graph/revision/evidence states shown are illustrative target capabilities; current storage contains immutable submitted tasks.
The focused v2 shows only plugin panel contents. The actual OpenCode session provides ambient context; do not duplicate its sidebar or conversation.

previousScreens.status: Rejected by user: too complicated and information scattered. Do not implement these layouts.

Subtle feature labels organize the list

layout.host: OpenCode native side-region Panel contribution, coexisting with conversation and existing LAZERS WebGPU GUI entry

tasks.divider: User-resizable horizontal splitter; list and inspector scroll independently
tasks.scopeDefault: Current routed session, including tasks owned by its plan and linked worker/subagent work
tasks.selectionKey: Canonical task ID, with explicit specification revision and attempt
tasks.narrow: Keep list above details; collapse secondary columns into a second line; allow detail expansion without replacing task state
tasks.scopePresentation: Session scope is inherited from the host. Put the project-view choice in the quiet view menu; no global scope or permanent scope toolbar.
tasks.stateKey: Server identity + canonical project identity + owning session ID. Preserve selection/filter/splitter state independently for each session.
tasks.sessionSwitch: Read reactive PanelProps.session/host context. Cancel old loads/subscriptions and reject late results; show only the new session's task data. The native panel render may remain mounted across a route switch.
tasks.membership: Use task/plan ownership and explicit links to worker sessions; do not move ownership when another session retries or views a task. Creator provenance alone is not a future ownership/graph model.

content: Timeline of state transitions and pending Architect decisions
Local inference status through the existing WebGPU contract when enabled
system.reference: Agent Radar live activity and drill-down, with runtime-owned task state as the source of truth
system.status: Future concepts saved under design/system-panel; user approved direction with narrow timeline correction. No scheduler implementation claimed.
system.layout: Narrow side panel with visualization above selected-run detail, separated by a horizontal resizable divider. No right-hand inspector column.
system.placement: Separate panel/command; do not add a prominent System tab to the focused task panel

activeDefault.history: Explicit history filter can retrieve all states; show hidden accepted count
activeDefault.selectedTaskFinishes: Keep its inspector and a completion notice until the user changes selection; update list counts without stealing focus

list.groups: Use the recorded plan/feature root and actual dependency topology. Sequential rows stay ordered; unambiguous parallel branches expand beneath their root. See execution-list.json for the current user-directed behavior.
list.sequential: Render stable admitted order and direct dependency references; do not infer a serial dependency from adjacent rows.
list.parallel: Accordion actual fork/join branches with lifecycle glyphs and a shared root lane. Runtime facts determine whether branches are eligible or actually concurrent; write/resource waits remain visible through compact references and selected detail.
list.writeConflicts: Explain serialization caused by overlapping write scopes even when there is no dependency edge
list.readiness: Default list uses a lifecycle glyph. Selected details explain its wait reason in one plain line; recorded lifecycle and other scheduling reasons are available in Details.
list.ordering: Stable feature groups and task order; avoid event-driven resorting while the user reads.
controls: Active view menu, including project-scope and history options
list.bulk: Bulk selection acts through runtime-validated commands with partial-failure reporting. Visual reordering never edits dependency edges.

acceptance: Required evidence or named human decision
Overall feature acceptance separate from individual task acceptance
activity: Consumed and remaining budgets with unavailable measurements shown as unknown
actions: Open worker session or result diff
Ask Architect with this task/revision attached
Respond to an actual user question
Request a new attempt, reschedule, repair, or revised plan through runtime commands when allowed
inspector.authority: Display only allowed actions returned by runtime capabilities. A UI action does not directly change lifecycle state. Acceptance is determined from evidence and policy; approval appears only for an actual unresolved human decision.

Activity: Durable outcome delivery and budget accounting

inspector.presentation: One continuous surface. No metadata grid, cards, inspector tabs, repeated status chips, or action toolbar by default. Runtime actions live in the selected task's overflow menu.

liveData.source: One canonical-project server read service shared by GUI RPC and Architect tools. The GUI request narrows to the routed session by default or explicitly selected current project; never an all-project/global query.
liveData.snapshot: Return task summaries, counts, graph relations, snapshot version/cursor, and server timestamp; detail loads by canonical ID/revision.
liveData.events: Publish plugin-owned task/graph/attempt/evidence changes after commit. Exact RPC method and event names are proposed implementation work.
liveData.raceHandling: Subscribe and buffer events around snapshot acquisition; apply only newer revisions; resync on gaps or reconnect. A live-only host stream is insufficient as a durable task ledger.
liveData.connection: Use only a small live indicator by default. Show a concise explicit stale/error message when disconnected; no routine timestamp/status footer.
liveData.continuity: Keep selected ID, keyboard focus, scroll anchor, filters and splitter ratio stable across updates. Cancel old project/detail requests so late responses cannot replace the current selection.
verification: Submit in another Desktop session and observe the same project panel update without refresh.
Disconnect/restart the host and verify stale indication, resubscription, full resync and no duplicate rows.
Accepted rows leave Active while selected details stay readable.
A graph dependency remains inspectable when its accepted predecessor is hidden.
A failed verification and bounded repair display distinct attempts and retained budget usage.
Switch sessions and projects while requests are pending; no late response, stale selection or event from the old scope may appear in the new view.
Project scope includes related sessions only in the current canonical project. No global task feed exists.

theme.requirement: The accepted focused panel must use OpenCode's current fonts and theme. The raster mockup is a layout reference, not a source of hardcoded colors or font choices.
theme.publicAPI: ctx.ui components follow the user's theme/fonts/language; ctx.appearance.mode() and font('mono') are reactive.
theme.components: Prefer ctx.ui controls and icons so native focus, theme, font, and interaction behavior are retained.

fonts.interface: Inherit the host UI font; custom buttons and inputs inherit typography too. Do not bundle fonts, hardcode Inter/system font stacks, or copy the image's typeface.
fonts.monospace: Use ctx.appearance.font('mono') reactively for task references, code, paths and commands. The public appearance getter exposes the mono font; use normal CSS inheritance for UI text.
fonts.scale: Keep the host's normal panel text scale and compact row density. The generated image's large pixel dimensions are not literal CSS font sizes.

theme.customStyles: Use inherited semantic host CSS variables for custom rows/surfaces. Do not freeze computed colors or maintain an independent light/dark palette.
theme.compatibility: CSS token names are verified against the pinned release's source, not a stable public theme-object guarantee. Isolate mappings and check on upgrades.
acceptance: Switch dark/light while Tasks is open; preserve selection, scroll, filters and splitter.
Switch between two named themes in the same mode; custom task rows and native controls both update.
Change OpenCode's monospace font with Tasks open; task references, code and paths update without reopening. UI labels continue inheriting host typography.
Text plus icons convey state in every theme; honor reduced motion and visible keyboard focus.

architectQueries.decision: Enable confined Code Mode for task investigation; the previous blanket execute restriction is not the intended final authority boundary.
architectQueries.current: lazers_list_tasks and lazers_get_task already exist as direct tools. List is limited to the newest 100 summaries and is not a complete overlap-search API. All three task tools currently set codemode:false, and Architect currently denies execute.
architectQueries.proposal: Expose typed, bounded query/get operations in Code Mode, with structured output and project-scoped permissions. Architect can query the current project across sessions for overlap while its default panel stays session-scoped. GUI and agent share the read service, without a shadow task store.
results: Scope overlap and relevant acceptance snippets
duplicateFlow: Query relevant existing tasks, including accepted history, before a genuinely new submission.
Retrieve promising candidates and compare intent, scope, acceptance and repository context.
Reuse the existing ID when the user is requesting the same known work.
When overlap is materially ambiguous, ask a focused question identifying the existing task and the differences.
Create separate work when the intent is distinct; revising existing scope uses an explicit versioned operation once implemented.
Submission idempotency still handles repeated logical calls; semantic overlap search does not establish exactly-once submission.
architectQueries.authority: Code Mode composes permitted tools and processes results. Runtime APIs continue to own admission, transitions, dependency validity, cancellation and budgets. Per-tool permission checks still run.
architectQueries.hostEvidence: Pinned Code Mode is an interpreter without direct process/filesystem/import access. OpenCode adds permission-checked fetch and routes inner tool calls through its normal executor. Support must be verified through Desktop before the live agent policy is changed.
architectQueries.noNewApprovalCeremony: Ask only when overlapping work creates a material intent/scope decision; a query result alone does not require user approval.

implementationBoundary.nextIncrement: A live task read API and native Tasks panel over persisted task records, including Code Mode query access and a concise overlap-investigation instruction. Extend the same contract as the real scheduler adds states/graphs/attempts.
implementationBoundary.currentState: Current records must appear as submitted with their real TaskSpec and context. Do not show fake runtime events, fabricate running states, or introduce a manual handoff workflow to compensate for the missing scheduler.
implementationBoundary.taskMethod: Have the Desktop Architect inspect this design and define the bounded implementation task before implementation. Mockup generation does not dispatch or implement it.
implementationBoundary.parallelWork: Preserve the other session's WebGPU implementation and integrate into the one existing GUI entry rather than creating another plugin package.
